known_mismatch.reason: strict_variables + `undef?.x.y ?? d` / `is defined`: the outer GetAttrExpression compiles the object of the inner null-safe node (the `$_vK = ...` short-circuit) before that node is compiled. Only that later compile propagates `ignore_strict_check` to the variable, so PHP throws `Variable "undef" does not exist.`. When the null-safe node is outermost (`undef?.x ?? d`) the flag arrives in time. twig-rs passes the null-safe node's own ignore_strict_check to its object. known_mismatch.reason: Wrong values: a null-safe chain in a function argument can inherit the short-circuit state of an earlier call's null-safe node. call() binds arguments through CallableArgumentsExtractor::extract_arguments(), which returns cloned Expr nodes that are dropped after the call. The null-safe state map is keyed by node address (null_safe_key()), so a later node allocated at a freed address gets `short_circuited: true` and loads a stale or unassigned local. Suspected: src/lltl/codegen.rs call() and null_safe_key(). Reproduction depends on allocation reuse, hence many calls; also affects filter arguments (`join`, `default`), not tests, macros or method arguments.

known_mismatch.reason: Known since the tooling round (cluster 3): a non-callable `has some`/`has every` operand. PHP says `Value of type bool is not callable` (zend_zval_type_name); twig-rs says `Value of type false is not callable`. Suspected: src/vm/arrow.rs invoke_value(), src/extension/runtime/arrays/callables.rs.
